title: Fanout of compiled circuit lists
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and $cs$ a finite list of Boolean circuit trees on $n$ variables. Suppose that, for every $c$ in $cs$, compiling $c$ after any acyclic gate list $gs$ appends a list of gates satisfying the single-circuit fanout conditions: old gate vertices are unused, every vertex of index at least $n$ is used at most once, any root of index at least $n$ is unused, each root is either an input vertex of index less than $n$ or a new vertex beyond the old gates, and every new vertex other than the root is used exactly once. Then for every acyclic initial gate list $gs$, compiling the whole list $cs$ appends some gate list $ext$ such that old gate vertices are unused, each vertex of index at least $n$ is used at most once, every listed root of index at least $n$ is unused, each listed root is either an input vertex of index less than $n$ or a new vertex beyond the old gates, and every new vertex not among the listed roots is used exactly once.
hypotheses_covered: $cs$ is a finite list of Boolean circuit trees on $n$ variables
Each circuit in $cs$ has the stated single-circuit compilation fanout property for every acyclic initial gate list
$gs$ is an acyclic initial gate list
